title: Task board status report
objective: Add assignee-aware task formatting and a concise board summary across the five-file dependency chain.
requirements: Every Task records an assignee name.
priorityLabel returns the uppercase label LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH.
formatTask returns [PRIORITY] title — assignee and appends a check mark when the task is complete.
formatTaskList preserves input order and returns one formatted task per line.
summarizeTasks starts with the total and completed counts, followed by the formatted task list when tasks exist.

files.task: Add the required assignee field to the Task contract.
requirements: Every Task records an assignee name.

owns.name: Task
owns.description: Defines the task identity, display fields, priority, completion state, and assignee.
owns.declaration: export interface Task { id: string; title: string; priority: "low" | "medium" | "high"; completed: boolean; assignee: string; }

skills.name: Contract discipline
skills.content: Preserve every existing Task property and add only the planned required property.

files.task: Return stable uppercase labels for every supported task priority.
requirements: priorityLabel returns the uppercase label LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH.

owns.name: priorityLabel
owns.description: Maps a task priority to its stable uppercase display label.

skills.name: Exhaustive domain mapping
skills.content: Handle every declared priority explicitly and do not add a fallback for values outside the Task contract.

files.task: Format one task with its uppercase priority, title, assignee, and completion state.
requirements: formatTask returns [PRIORITY] title — assignee and appends a check mark when the task is complete.

owns.name: formatTask
owns.description: Formats one task with its priority, title, assignee, and completion marker.

skills.name: TypeScript module boundaries
skills.content: Use import type for type-only dependencies and NodeNext .js specifiers for relative imports.

constraints: Call exactly `priorityLabel(task.priority)` to obtain the display label.
Use an em dash between the title and assignee.
Append the check mark only for completed tasks.

files.task: Render tasks in their supplied order using the shared task formatter.
requirements: formatTaskList preserves input order and returns one formatted task per line.

owns.name: formatTaskList
owns.description: Formats tasks in supplied order with one task on each line.
owns.declaration: export function formatTaskList(tasks: readonly Task[]): string;

skills.name: Stable collection formatting
skills.content: Do not sort or mutate the input array. Join the shared formatter results with a newline and add no bullet prefix.

constraints: Call exactly `formatTask(task)` for every task in supplied order.
Return an empty string for an empty task array.
Do not duplicate the single-task formatting logic.

files.task: Produce the board-level count summary and append the formatted task list when non-empty.
requirements: summarizeTasks starts with the total and completed counts, followed by the formatted task list when tasks exist.

owns.name: summarizeTasks
owns.description: Builds the board-level total and completion summary followed by the formatted list.
owns.declaration: export function summarizeTasks(tasks: readonly Task[]): string;

skills.name: Summary composition
skills.content: Count completed tasks without mutating input. Use the exact header form {total} tasks · {complete} complete and add the formatted list on the next line only when tasks exist.

constraints: Call exactly `formatTaskList(tasks)` for the list portion.
